audit.name: Oldowan flaking
audit.ageGap: root (no prerequisites)
audit.effectRationale: Sharp flakes and hammerstones open carcasses and long bones: marrow and scavenged meat let a band ride out lean spells.
audit.rationale: Root of the knapping family; unchanged. Effect is food-security from butchery and marrow, not tool output.

audit.name: Prepared-core (Levallois)
audit.ageGap: root (no prerequisites)
audit.effectRationale: Prepared cores yield predetermined, portable blanks: groups carry a toolkit instead of tethering to a stone source, so movers range further.
audit.rationale: Levallois is a prepared-core refinement of hard-hammer flaking; making knapping_oldowan its prerequisite gives the knapping family one root instead of two unrelated roots (both A1, Oldowan ~2.6 Mya precedes ~300 kya). Not a chronology edge: the prepared core is literally flaking applied with foresight.

audit.name: Blade production

prereqAssessment.why: Blade cores are a further development of prepared-core reduction.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Prismatic blade cores give several times more cutting edge per kilogram of flint: quarrying and working stone yields more usable product per worker.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Pressure flaking
audit.ageGap: root (no prerequisites)
audit.effectRationale: Thin, symmetrical projectile points (Solutrean, Clovis) make big-game kills more reliable, so lean seasons kill fewer.
audit.rationale: Currently an isolated root and leaf. The Blombos evidence ties the two directly: silcrete was heat-treated precisely so it could be pressure-flaked (~75 kya, after heat treatment at ~164 kya). Pressure retouch of a fine blank presupposes improving the stone first. Remains a deliberate leaf (finishing technique).

audit.name: Heat treatment of stone

prereqAssessment.why: Controlled heating in a sand bed under a fire is the method.
The heated stone is then knapped by prepared-core methods; Levallois (~300 kya) precedes Pinnacle Point (~164 kya).

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms. fire_making's emerged text dates itself by this very node (~164 kya); the edge is logical, the shared date is fire_making's labelling.
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from energy
audit.effectRationale: Heating poor silcrete or chert makes it flake cleanly: more of the quarried stone becomes usable, and the resulting edges are sharper.
audit.rationale: Keep. Becomes a non-leaf if pressure_flaking takes it as prerequisite.

audit.name: Microliths and composite tools

prereqAssessment.why: Microliths are useless unless set in a haft.
Microliths are snapped and backed blade segments.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Replaceable geometric inserts: a worn or broken segment is swapped and the sickle or knife lives on, so equipped tools last longer.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Ground-edge axe

prereqAssessment.why: Ground axes are first roughed out by flaking, then ground; flaking is the needed predecessor.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms. Dated ~44-35 kya (Australia, Japan) - earlier than grinding_stone's own ~30 kya date, so grinding_stone is correctly NOT a prerequisite.
audit.effectRationale: A resharpenable ground-edge felling axe makes heavy timber work feasible: logging is unlocked and dwellings take less labour.
audit.rationale: Keep; live unlock activity.logging plus a housing labour effect from efficient woodworking.

audit.name: Compound adhesives
audit.ageGap: root (no prerequisites)
audit.effectRationale: Load-bearing compound binders keep inserts and heads seated under impact: tools fail less and transmit more force.
audit.rationale: Root; keep. fire_making is NOT added despite heat-processed bitumen: its node is dated ~164 kya, after this node's ~200 kya, which would break chronology.

audit.name: Birch-bark tar

prereqAssessment.why: Birch tar is the manufactured successor of natural binders.
Dry distillation needs controlled heating without oxygen.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms. Must-held fire_making is dated ~164 kya against this node's ~200 kya (Campitello): fire_making's emerged text is anchored on heat treatment, not on fire control (~400 kya+). Edge kept; date text to be fixed in the energy group.
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from energy
audit.effectRationale: Tar is an adhesive and a wood and bark preservative and sealant: treated timber and bark structures last longer.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Composite hafting

prereqAssessment.why: Compound adhesive is the other half of a load-bearing haft.
Sinew or fibre binding of the haft.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms. cordage's direct evidence (~50 kya) postdates secure hafting (~200 kya); cordage's emerged text records an evidential floor ('older inferred'). Edge kept.
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from industry
audit.effectRationale: A precision-fitted socket or tang turns a hand-held edge into a lever: hafted axes, adzes and hoes multiply the gain from every tool.
audit.rationale: Keep. unit.spearmen requires it but units are not live (M7), so the realized effect is the tool-yield operand.

audit.name: Pigment processing

prereqAssessment.why: Blombos ochre was processed on grindstones; the edge is the actual technique.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms. grinding_stone is dated by plant processing (~30 kya) while ochre grinding is ~100 kya; edge is logical, date text is grinding_stone's.
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from agriculture
audit.effectRationale: Ground ochre for body marking and shared symbolic display builds group identity, damping the build-up of grievance; also preserves hides.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Bone and antler tools

prereqAssessment.why: Groove-and-splinter bone working needs burins struck from blades.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms. Katanda harpoons (~90 kya) predate the widespread blade date; knapping_blade's text carries the earlier African ~70 kya figure, near enough.
audit.effectRationale: Eyed needles and awls make tailored, layered clothing; less exposure lowers baseline mortality (harpoons also add fish).
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Open-fired pottery

prereqAssessment.why: Coil building and container design come from basketry; many early pots carry basket impressions.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: basketry A1 (gap 1); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from industry
audit.effectRationale: Sealed pots keep stores from damp and vermin; boiling makes gruels that wean and feed children through shortages.
audit.costConcern: 2,490 is high for an A2 trunk node next to kiln 4,180 and potters_wheel 440; leave to the per-Age scale.
audit.rationale: Keep; live recipe plus storage and child-feeding effects. Fire is baseline (baseline.fire), so no fire_making edge is needed.

audit.name: Updraft kiln

prereqAssessment.why: Kiln chambers are built of mudbrick and clay.
The kiln is an enclosed version of pottery firing.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from construction
audit.effectRationale: Live unlock building.kiln; the kiln's own building effects carry the gameplay, so no operand is added.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Fast wheel (throwing)

prereqAssessment.why: Throwing presupposes ceramic know-how.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Thrown pottery at scale is a full-time trade: the wheel supports a larger specialist artisan class.
audit.rationale: Deliberate leaf (a craft specialisation). Emerged ~3,500 BCE sits on the A2/A3 boundary; Age kept.

audit.name: Native copper working

prereqAssessment.why: Annealing between hammerings needs fire.
Native copper is worked with hammerstones and grinding, a ground-stone skill set.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: fire_making A1 (gap 1), ground_stone_early A1 (gap 1); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from energy
audit.effectRationale: Cold-hammered and annealed copper awls, pins and small blades: a first metal edge for equipped workers.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Copper smelting

prereqAssessment.why: Knowing copper as a material; OR branch.
Furnace temperatures and atmosphere control come from kilns.
Malachite and azurite were ground as pigment before they were smelted; the OR alternative is a real pathway.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: ochre_processing A1 (gap 1); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.effectRationale: Smelted metal can be resharpened and remelted instead of discarded: tools last longer; smithy unlocked.
audit.newPrereq: kiln_updraft AND charcoal AND (copper_native OR ochre_processing)
audit.rationale: Reduction smelting needs charcoal: its carbon monoxide is the reductant and a wood fire cannot reach or hold reducing conditions. The node's own description says 'in a charcoal fire'. charcoal (A2, ~5,500 BCE) predates smelting (~5,000 BCE); charcoal already feeds iron_bloomery on the same grounds.

audit.name: Open-mould casting

prereqAssessment.why: Casting needs molten metal from smelting.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Cast copper axe heads are reproducible: felling and quarrying crews are better equipped.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Native gold and silver

prereqAssessment.why: Same cold-working and annealing techniques as native copper.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Gold and silver as prestige goods and an early store of value: exchange is easier, so price gaps close faster.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Arsenical bronze

prereqAssessment.why: Smelted from arsenical ores in the same furnaces.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: copper_smelting A2 (gap 1); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.effectRationale: Arsenic-bearing copper work-hardens: harder edges without tin trade.
audit.rationale: Deliberate leaf: the no-tin alloy path. Emerged ~4,000 BCE predates the A3 window, as do several A3 materials nodes placed by maturity; Age not moved.

audit.name: Tin bronze

prereqAssessment.why: Tin ore (cassiterite) must be found before it can be alloyed; copper smelting comes through this atom.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: A reproducible 10% tin alloy is harder and work-hardens: edges hold far longer than copper; bronze casting unlocked.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Two-piece and closed-mould casting

prereqAssessment.why: Closed moulds extend open-mould casting.
Bronze's fluidity fills thin bivalve moulds for socketed forms.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: casting_open A2 (gap 1); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.effectRationale: Bivalve moulds turn out socketed sickles and hoes that stay on their hafts: each farmer harvests and tills more.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Lost-wax casting

prereqAssessment.why: Investment casting needs pouring skills.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: casting_open A2 (gap 1); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.effectRationale: Cult statuary and votive objects in any shape sustain shared ritual and display.
audit.rationale: Deliberate leaf (art and ritual metalwork).

audit.name: Sheet metalwork

prereqAssessment.why: Raising sheet relies on bronze's work-hardening and annealing behaviour.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Raised bronze cauldrons and buckets let households and feasts cook and redistribute stores in bulk; armour use waits for M7.
audit.rationale: Keep. Its main capability (sheet armour) is military and not live; the realized effect is a modest food-handling one.

audit.name: Shaft mining

prereqAssessment.why: The node models ore mining for metal; flint mines predate it but are not its capability.
Shoring, stone-lined galleries and spoil handling.

audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Fired brick

Moulded standard bricks.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: kiln_updraft A2 (gap 1), mudbrick A2 (gap 1); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from construction
audit.effectRationale: Kiln-fired, waterproof brick: drains and sewers unlocked, and buildings stand far longer.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Glaze and faience

Alkali flux (natron, plant ash, salts) is the glass-forming ingredient.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: kiln_updraft A2 (gap 1), salt_extraction A2 (gap 1); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from food
audit.effectRationale: A vitreous coat seals porous ceramic: glazed jars keep stored food and oil from seeping and spoiling.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Core-formed vessels are palace-workshop products: glassmaking supports another specialist artisan class.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Bloomery iron

Shaft furnace temperature and atmosphere control.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: charcoal A2 (gap 2), kiln_updraft A2 (gap 2); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from energy
audit.effectRationale: Landmark: ore is everywhere, so iron hoes, ploughshares and axes reach ordinary farmers; equipped workers gain much more from tools.
audit.rationale: Keep. copper_smelting (the smelting principle) is not added: the A4 sweep already requires all of A2, so the edge would be redundant.

audit.name: Carburized steel

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Carbon-hardened edges outlast soft wrought iron: tools need replacing less often.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Quench hardening

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Martensite-hard picks, wedges and axe edges cut rock and timber faster.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Tempering

prereqAssessment.why: Tempering relieves quench brittleness.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Tough and hard: tempered tools neither chip nor bend, so they last and work better.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Wootz crucible steel

prereqAssessment.why: Sealed refractory crucibles fired at high temperature.
Carbon absorption principle.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: kiln_updraft A2 (gap 2); fine (not a reason to change). ~300 BCE sits in the A5 window although placed in A4; left (moving changes sweep cohorts and it has no dependents).
audit.effectRationale: Compact, high-value crucible-steel ingots were a staple of long-distance trade (South India to Persia and Syria).
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Pattern welding

prereqAssessment.why: Laminates steel with iron.

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Forge-welding a steel edge onto a soft iron body (piling, steeling) makes economical edged tools from small, uneven blooms.
audit.rationale: Deliberate leaf. Effect stated as the economic side of forge-welding (steeled tools), not the sword.

audit.name: Cast and mosaic glass

prereqAssessment.why: Successor technique of core-formed glass.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: glass_core A3 (gap 1); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.effectRationale: Cast and mosaic glass vessels are a luxury workshop industry employing specialist glassworkers.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Hydraulic concrete

prereqAssessment.why: Burnt lime is the binder.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: lime_plaster A2 (gap 3); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from construction
audit.effectRationale: Hydraulic concrete strengthens with age and sets underwater: durable buildings, and artificial harbour moles that cut shipping costs.
audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.name: Glassblowing

The blowpipe is an iron tube.

audit.ageGap: earlier-Age atoms: glass_blown_precursor A4 (gap 1), iron_bloomery A4 (gap 1); fine (not a reason to change)
audit.effectRationale: Cheap blown bottles and flasks became standard containers for oil, wine and medicine: stocks move to market faster.

audit.name: Window glass

audit.ageGap: same Age for all atoms
audit.effectRationale: Glazed windows let homes, baths and sickrooms keep heat while admitting light: less cold-season illness.
audit.rationale: Keep. The description says 'cast' panes; glass_blown_precursor (casting) would be the narrower atom, but cheapness came from the blowing industry, so the edge stands.

Pouring into moulds.
Iron ore smelting.

audit.rationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

audit.costConcern: 310 is the cheapest A2 node; acceptable for a narrow regional craft.

audit.name: Spectacles

audit.name: Water-powered blast furnace

Iron smelting.

audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from energy, industry
audit.effectRationale: Water-driven bellows make cast iron in quantity in Europe: iron plentiful enough for fully ironed tools.
audit.rationale: Replace crank_connecting_rod with trip_hammer (A5, ~40 BCE; prereq water_mill): water power with cams is the mechanism the node is named for, and the crank (general ~1,400) postdates the node's earliest date (~1,150).

audit.crossTree: none (technology atoms only); cross-lane atoms from industry

newNodes.name: Tinplate
newNodes.emerged: ~1,350 CE Bohemia and the Upper Palatinate (hammered iron sheet dipped in tin; date approximate); 1720 CE Pontypool, Wales (rolled tinplate)
newNodes.prereqRationale: iron_bloomery: the base metal is iron sheet. sheet_metal: hammering metal to thin sheet, and (through tin_bronze) knowledge of tin as a metal. trip_hammer: water-driven tilt hammers beat the iron to sheet in the Bohemian and Saxon works. All dated well before the node.
newNodes.desc: Thin iron sheet coated with molten tin so it will not rust: light, cheap, sealable boxes, canisters and kitchenware, and later the tin can.
newNodes.distinctFrom: sheet_metal is hammered bronze for vessels and armour; tinplate is rust-proofed iron sheet for sealed containers (the missing bridge to canning).

newNodes.name: Crucible cast steel
newNodes.emerged: ~1,740 CE Sheffield (Huntsman melts blister steel in coke-fired clay crucibles)
newNodes.prereqRationale: coke: a coke-fired draught furnace is what reaches the ~1,600 C needed to melt steel (coke 1709 CE precedes). steel_carburized: the charge is cementation (blister) steel, the tree's carburized-steel node.
newNodes.desc: Blister steel melted in sealed clay crucibles and cast into ingots: uniform, slag-free tool steel for files, springs, razors and edge tools.
newNodes.distinctFrom: wootz is small-batch South Indian crucible steel for blades without coke; this is coke-fired, homogeneous cast tool steel made in quantity for machine and edge tools.

newNodes.name: Galvanized corrugated iron
newNodes.emerged: 1829 CE London (Palmer's corrugated iron sheet); 1837 CE Paris (Sorel's hot-dip galvanizing patent)
newNodes.prereqRationale: puddling: cheap wrought iron rolled to sheet (1784 CE precedes). brass_calamine: the tree's only zinc-metallurgy node (zinc ore and zinc vapour); metallic zinc distillation (Champion 1738 CE) has no node, so this is the nearest correct atom.
newNodes.desc: Iron sheet dipped in molten zinc and rolled into corrugations: a light, stiff, rust-resistant roof and wall cladding shipped flat and nailed up anywhere.
newNodes.distinctFrom: portland_cement replaces timber in walls and foundations; galvanized iron replaces shingle and thatch roofing that must be renewed, chiefly cutting upkeep.

findings: Dependency changes proposed: 4 (knapping_levallois +knapping_oldowan; pressure_flaking +heat_treatment_stone; copper_smelting +charcoal; blast_furnace_water crank_connecting_rod -> trip_hammer). All others kept.
Every materials node now ends with a registry effect or a live unlock; 14 nodes have live unlocks (kiln_updraft and ore_prospecting rely on the unlock alone).

Tool operands carry most of the lane's early value: production.toolYieldBonusMax sums to 0.32 and toolWearPerEquippedFarmerPerYear to 0.29 across the lane (new nodes included), well under the caps (1.0 / 0.8); research.researchPointsCoefficient reaches 0.15 of its 0.3 cap from this lane alone (spectacles, glass_lead, metallography, nanotechnology, brass_calamine), so the integrator should watch the cross-lane total.

Date-text inversions on must-held edges come from other lanes' emerged strings, not from wrong edges: fire_making (~164 kya, anchored on heat treatment) under birch_tar (~200 kya); cordage (~50 kya direct floor) under hafting (~200 kya); grinding_stone (~30 kya plant milling) under ochre_processing (~100 kya). Fix the texts in the energy, industry and agriculture groups.

Several A3 and A4 materials nodes have emerged dates outside their Age window (arsenical_bronze, lost_wax, glass_glaze, mining_shaft ~4,000 BCE in A3; wootz and pattern_welding ~300 BCE in A4). They are placed by maturity, and moving them would change sweep cohorts, so no move is proposed.

Cross-group bridges to raise with other lanes: canning (food) should require the new tinplate; petroleum_refining (science) should require percussion_drilling; telescope or celestial_navigation could take brass_calamine (instrument brass).
Gap left open: metallic zinc distillation (Zawar ~1,200 CE; Champion 1738 CE) has no node; galvanized_iron uses brass_calamine as the nearest zinc atom.
The A7 materials lane had only 2 nodes (coke, glass_lead); crucible_cast_steel fills the steel step between coke (1709) and puddling (1784).

Pacing: asteroid_mining (39,780) costs less than composites and nanotechnology (66,910); pottery_open_fired (2,490) is high for A2 next to potters_wheel_fast (440). Leave these to the per-(tree, Age) scale.
Military capabilities in this lane (sheet armour, pattern-welded blades, unit.spearmen via hafting) are not live; their nodes carry modest economic effects until M7.
